sentences.text: 2. Case of the appellant in brief is that, the Estate Officer / respondent No.2 initiated proceedings under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971 against this appellant and others by issuing a notice under Sub-Section (1) of Section 5 alleging that, the appellant has encroached upon the railway property to the extent of 280.35 sq. mtrs. and constructed (G+2) floor building at Benniganahalli.

entities.text: Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The appellant was called upon to respond to all material questions and present evidence before the Estate Officer on a specified date.

3. In response to the notice, the appellant appeared before the Estate Officer and filed objections and produced relevant documents including sale deeds, katha extracts and building sanction plan issued by the BBMP.

4. The Estate Officer by impugned order, allowed the claim of the South Western Railway,
Bengaluru i.e., respondent No.1 and directed the appellant and others to vacate the encroached portion of the land within the stipulated period.

5. Aggrieved by the impugned order, the appellant has preferred the present appeal contending that,
the Estate Officer failed to appreciate the facts, particularly, regarding the appellant's title over the disputed land, which he acquired under the registered gift deed dated 20.12.2019 from his mother.
The appellant further contended that, he is in possession and enjoyment of the property by paying taxes to the BBMP.

He has claimed that, his predecessor Ramaiah S/o. Devanna purchased property measuring 19 guntas in Sy.No.4 of Benniganahalli Village under the registered sale deed dated 11.08.1971 from B.S.Krishnamurthy S/o. Late Kantappa and pleaded about flow of title to the property.
After obtaining necessary permission from the BBMP, building has been constructed.
The appellant contended that, the Estate Officer / respondent No.2 failed to consider the objections properly and erred in passing the impugned order.

6. In the year 1991, when the Estate Officer issued similar notice, his predecessor Nagappa had filed W.P.No.19283/1991, wherein, the Hon'ble High Court directed the respondents to consider the objections and to pass suitable order.
Thereafter, for a period of 25 years, the respondents have kept quite and now they have initiated the present proceedings.
Hence, the appellant has perfected his title to the property by way of adverse possession as he is in unobstructed possession and enjoyment of the property for a period more than 12 years.
Therefore, the appellant prayed to set aside the impugned order by allowing this appeal.

7. The respondents filed detailed objections to the appeal contending that, the land to the extent of 1 acre 13 guntas in Sy.No.4 of Benniganahalli Village was notified for formation of Bengaluru to Salem Railway Line Project in the year 1962.

During inspection by railway authorities, determined the actual encroachment on the railway property in Sy.Nos.4 & 5 and found that, the property in Raju vs The Divisional Railway Manager on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73422784/
2 appellants' possession was within the Sy.No.4 of Benniganahalli Village and was encroached upon.

entities.text: Raju vs The Divisional Railway Manager on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondents asserted that, the appellants unauthorisedly constructed the building.

Therefore,
the Estate Officer / respondent No.2 issued notice under Sec.4(1) of the Act and after following due procedure, passed the impugned order.
Further, it is contended that, appellant has not made out grounds to interfere with the impugned order, hence, prayed to dismiss the appeal.
8. Case record was summoned from the office of the Estate Officer and reviewed.
Heard arguments and perused the entire materials on record.

Now, the points that arise for my consideration are as follows:
1. Whether the appellant has established any grounds to interfere with the impugned order exercising the power conferred under Section 9(1) of the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971 ?
2. What order ?
9. My findings on the above points are as under :-
 Point No.1 : In the Negative,
 Point No.2 : As per final order;
for the following :-
 REASONS 10. POINT NO.1: In an appeal filed under Section 9(1) of the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971, the Court's power to scrutinize the order passed by the authorized officer under Section 5 of the Act, is limited.

Unless, it is found from the fact of the record and order that, the order is perverse or passed without applying the mind by ignoring due procedure and principles of natural justice, the Court refrains from interfering.
11. The special enactment aims to protect public property from land grabbers.
In this context, the facts of the present case must be appreciated before recording any findings on the legality of the impugned order.
According to the respondents, an extent of 1 acre 13  guntas of land in Sy.No.4 of Benniganahalli Village was notified for the Railway Project in 1962.
The appellant claimed to be in possession and enjoyment of the house property measuring 18 x 30 feet, which was gifted to him by his mother Pallani under the gift deed dated 20.12.2019.
As per the case of the appellant, his predecessor Ramaiah purchased 19 guntas of land in Sy.No.4 of Benniganahalli Village on 11.08.1971.
Thereafter, it was divided among the children of Ramaiah.

Therefore, it is clear that, the sale deed, subsequent division and git deed in favour of appellant are subject to the notification of Raju vs The Divisional Railway Manager on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73422784/
3 the year 1962, notifying of the land in Sy.No.4 for the Railway.

sentences.text: 12. The appellant has contended that, BBMP sanctioned plan for construction of building on the disputed land and he is paying taxes to the BBMP.

As argued by the learned counsel for the respondents, when there is a bar under any special statute to own or construct any building in a notified area or land, merely because the local authority issued no objection certificate or sanctioned the construction plan, it would not confer any right to claim lawful possession over such property.
In this context, it is relevant to refer to the circulars / notifications issued by the Central Government to protect public property.

The Government of India - Ministry of Railway issued a notification dated 25.06.2015, prescribing procedures for issuing No Objection Certificates for construction /
redevelopment of Government and private buildings on land adjoining Railway boundaries.
As per the circular / notification, the Railway's NOC is required for construction within 30 meters from the Railway boundary, as per para 827 of IRWM.
Therefore, no authority can grant permission to construct within the buffer zone or boundary of Railway tracks.

13. The respondents produced a re-survey joint sketch and report prepared by the ADLR dated 03.09.2021, which shows that, the appellant's construction was within the acquired land and prohibited boundary.
The appellant produced photographs showing that, the building extended to the border of the Railway track.

It is well-settled law, as held by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Bombay Swadeshi Stores Vs. State Bank of Mysore, reported in ILR 1989 KAR 2506,
that, the primary considerations for the authority and the appellate authority in cases of public premises encroachment are whether the premises are public and whether the occupant is unauthorized.

entities.text: Bombay Swadeshi Stores Vs. State Bank of Mysore, reported in ILR 1989 KAR 2506
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If these questions are answered affirmatively, no further consideration is required.
The records indicate that, the Estate Officer issued notice before initiating proceedings.
The appellant duly appeared and presented documents and the Estate Officer passed the impugned order after considering all contentions.

14. Although, the appellant has set up a title regarding the land he allegedly encroached upon, the argument that, title disputes cannot be decided by the Estate Officer in summary proceedings is persuasive.
However, allowing such a defence could undermine the purpose of the special statute designed to protect public property.
Allowing parties to claim title to delay proceedings would defeat the statute's objective.
Even if a local authority issued a sanction plan contrary to the statute, it would not confer any rights to an unauthorized occupant.

Moreover, as the sale deed / gift deed relied upon by appellant is subsequent to the Government's acquisition for Railway project, they cannot claim to protect their possession based on such documents.
15. The appellant contends that, BMRCL awarded compensation in favour of Nagappa on 24.01.2019.
The land in question and the land acquired by BMRCL are different.

As per the joint survey conducted by ADLR and other authorities, the land in dispute where the house of the appellant situated comes within the property belongs to the Railway Department, hence, awarding compensation by BMRCL to some property near to disputed property is not a ground to hold that,
the land in dispute belongs to the appellant.

4 16.

sentences.text: Further, the appellant contends that, after the order of the Hon'ble High Court in W.P.No.19283/1991, the respondents kept quite for a long period, hence, the appellant has perfected his title to the property in dispute by way of adverse possession as he is in continuous possession and enjoyment of the property for more than 12 years.
To claim adverse possession, the appellant has to admit the property belongs to the respondents.
If the appellant admit that, the property belongs to the respondents, then admittedly, from the year 1991, the respondents are taking steps to recover land in dispute.

Further, to claim adverse possession against the Government property,
continuous possession of 12 years is not sufficient.
The survey conducted on 03.09.2021 by the government authorities is presumed to be known to the appellant since the survey is conducted in respect of disputed land.
Hence, the appellant cannot plead ignorance about the said survey.
Looking from any angle, this Court do not find any good grounds to interfere with the impugned order as there is no merit in the appeal.
Accordingly, I answer point No.1 is in the Negative.

17. POINT NO.2:- For the aforementioned discussions, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The appeal filed by the appellant under Section 9(1) of the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act 1977, is dismissed with cost.
